pr_title: Check Tessie scopes to fix startup bug
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
If a user hasnt granted Tessie permission to energy scopes it causes a setup error due to the way that the products API works. This PR implements the bare minimum of Scope checking to avoid triggering this failure.

Please beta hotfix

https://github.com/Teslemetry/python-tesla-fleet-api/compare/v0.6.1...v0.6.2

Which scopes have you given Tessie? I suspect I know what's going wrong but it would be good to confirm.

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/17516011/e16fbf7a-4334-4235-8f3b-8b36d0b5033f)

Just the profile and vehicle scopes

So fun fact, even though you haven't provided access to your energy data, the Tesla products endpoint returns details about all your energy products.

Thankfully James from Tessie added an API for me to check scopes so a fix is going in to respect your scope choices and not add energy products when you haven't granted the scope.

review_comments:
This IMHO is not a good pattern, the problem with this, is that users have no idea why information is missing.

We should guide them to set things up correctly.

So should we trigger a re-auth flow to guide them through the process? Or a repair issue with a repair flow guiding them to provide the needed scopes?

It's not a repair issue if a user has chosen to not provide that scope to Tessie, many people do this by choice.

I do guess they could then choose to ignore it, but I assumed I should respect the choice they already made when signing up.

Aah check, ok the scope is further upstream 👍 

That makes sense, thanks for the context 👍
What are the possible errors that can return? Is it justified that the ConfigEnteyNotReady is used here?

The possible errors:

https://github.com/Teslemetry/python-tesla-fleet-api/blob/main/tesla_fleet_api/exceptions.py

Is Config Entry Not Ready justified, I believe so, otherwise the entities won't work at all.

Also this code block isn't not new in this PR and unrelated to the issue I'm fixing.
